plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to zero.
Trim broad index (SPY) to 20% to reduce concentration and increase cash.
Add to income ETF (QQQI) to 25% for stability.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall risk.
A significant cash buffer is maintained for safety.
conservative.read: This conservative approach aims for lower, steadier returns around 1.5% per month. The focus is on capital preservation with reduced drawdown risk. Expect slower growth compared to other modes.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to low single digits.
Reduce semiconductor (MUU) and AI (METU) leverage.
Trim broad index (SPY) to 20% to reduce concentration.
Add a new quality tech name (DDOG) at 4%.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth opportunities.
A moderate cash buffer is maintained.
balanced.read: This balanced mode targets around 2.5% monthly growth with a risk-first approach. It reduces leverage and concentration while adding a quality name. Drawdowns are expected to be moderate.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and semiconductor/AI leverage (MUU, METU).
Trim broad index (SPY) to 20% to free up capital.
Add a new high-conviction tech name (DDOG) at 6%.
This aggressive plan aims for higher growth by increasing leverage and concentration.
A smaller cash buffer is maintained, increasing overall portfolio volatility.
Strict stop discipline is crucial due to amplified risk.
aggressive.read: This aggressive mode targets around 4% monthly growth, accepting significantly higher potential drawdowns. It leans into leverage and concentration, especially with leveraged ETFs. Daily rebalancing of leveraged ETFs can impact performance, and losses can be amplified quickly.

plan: Sell all high-beta and leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to zero.
Trim broad index (SPY) to 20% to increase cash holdings.
Increase income ETF (QQQI) to 30% for steady distributions.
This plan prioritizes generating monthly income over growth.
It aims for low volatility and capital preservation.
Distributions are variable and NAV can still decline.
income.read: This income-focused mode targets around 1% monthly return through distributions, prioritizing stability. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leverage and high-beta names. While aiming for cash-like income, the Net Asset Value (NAV) can still fall in market downturns.
